To calculate the minimum area per molecule ($A_{min}$), we first determine the number of surfactant molecules per unit area and then find the reciprocal. 

**1. Calculate the number of molecules per square centimeter:**
Given the maximum surface excess ($\Gamma_{max}$) and Avogadro's number ($N_A$):
$\Gamma_{max} = 3.4268 \times 10^{-10} \text{ mol/cm}^2$
$N_A \approx 6.02214076 \times 10^{23} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Number of molecules per cm$^2$ = $\Gamma_{max} \times N_A$
Number of molecules = $(3.4268 \times 10^{-10}) \times (6.02214076 \times 10^{23})$
$= 2.063667 \times 10^{14} \text{ molecules/cm}^2$

**2. Calculate area per molecule in cm$^2$:**
$A_{min} = \frac{1}{\text{Number of molecules per cm}^2}$
$A_{min} = \frac{1}{2.063667 \times 10^{14}} = 4.84574 \times 10^{-15} \text{ cm}^2/\text{molecule}$

**3. Convert to square nanometers (nm$^2$):**
There are $10^7$ nm in a cm, meaning $1 \text{ cm}^2 = (10^7)^2 \text{ nm}^2 = 10^{14} \text{ nm}^2$.
$A_{min} \text{ in nm}^2 = 4.84574 \times 10^{-15} \text{ cm}^2 \times 10^{14} \text{ nm}^2/\text{cm}^2 = 0.484574 \text{ nm}^2$

**4. Convert to square Angstroms (Å$^2$):**
There are $10 \text{ \AA}$ in $1 \text{ nm}$, meaning $1 \text{ nm}^2 = (10)^2 \text{ \AA}^2 = 100 \text{ \AA}^2$.
$A_{min} \text{ in \AA}^2 = 0.484574 \text{ nm}^2 \times 100 \text{ \AA}^2/\text{nm}^2 = 48.4574 \text{ \AA}^2$
